steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Place sliced potatoes and sliced onions in the prepared dish; mix gently. Cover potatoes and onions with cheese. Fill the dish with milk halfway. Place butter in several places over cheese. Place pork chops on top. Season with salt and pepper.

Bake in the preheated oven until potatoes are tender, about 60 minutes, turning pork chops over halfway through cooking. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of meat should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Scalloped Potatoes and Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Pork chops bake over cheesy scalloped potatoes and onions until tender in this comforting, family-friendly casserole that’s easy to make.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely wonderful. I scaled it back to 3 servings & also took others advice about microwaving the potatoes 1st, I did it for about 5 minutes. I also left the peel on & sliced them that way. I took another persons advice & mixed the potatoes, cheese & onions in a bowl, put them on the bottom, poured milk over top and put pats of butter in as well. Then placed the chops over all that. I also poured a little bit of milk over the chops. Halfway through, I pulled the chops off, stirred the potatoes & put the chops back on making sure I flipped them. I used a lot of pepper (I am not a big salt fan). I also noticed it a little "watery" after the hour, so I left them in there a bit longer & took some of the juices and put over the chops. I think I may have used a little too much butter, but my fiancee who is SOOOOOOOOO picky about food, really enjoyed this. He voluntarily said, "This is something you can make again, this is really good"

We've been making a dish like this for over 40 years. Our 7 kids grew-up on it, and they made it
for their kids. We always precook the potatoes about 10 minutes, season and brown the steaks or chops with a little salt & pepper, garlic powder and
a tad of ground savory. We use a can of cream of mushroom and celery soup, and 2 cans of milk. Mix the soup and milk together, then in the baking dish, mix the soup mixture with the potatoes. Nesle the chops into the potatoes, so they are almost covered in the soup mix. Bake covered until the potatoes are tender and meat juices run clear. That's our version of scalloped potatoes and pork chops!

I love this receipe. I use a mix of cheddar, harvarti, and jarlsberg cheeses. I also use cream instead of milk. Next time, however, I will microwave the potatoes as many have suggested. I have made this dish many times (without the chops) and always have crunchy potatoes.

This turned out amazing after several changes that i got from other reviews. I put the potatoes in the microwave for 5 minutes after slicing. Add the onions and milk to the potatoes after, in a separate bowl. I seasoned the chops with salt, pepper, and dried minced garlic and pan seared them. I put the chops on the bottom of the casserole dish and added the potato mixture on top. Put spoonfuls of butter on top of the potatoes and topped the whole thing with cheese. Covered the dish with foil for half an hour at 350. Was still worried about the potatoes, so I stirred the potatoes and bumped the oven to 375. Back in for half an hour, uncovered. Everything came out perfect.

I had tried this recipe exactly as it was written but like everyone else the pork chops dried out before the potatoes were done. So I decided to modify it a little. First I browned my chops and seasoned them with garlic and herb mrs. dash. Then I put a layer of potatoes in the bottom of my pan adding the pork chops on top. I sauteed my onions before mixing them in the milk and I used cream of chicken soup for a little extra flavoring. I also put a layer of mild cheddar cheese on top of the chops with a few dabs of butter. Then I put another layer of potatoes on top of that along with a little more butter. I poured the milk mixture over top of everything just enough to make sure that the potatoes are covered. I baked it on 350 for 90 minutes then added the layer of cheese on top and baked it for another 30 minutes. The chops were so tender they fell apart taking them out of the pan and the potatoes were tender and the sauce was thick and creamy. Everyone has different tastes when it comes to cooking but I fed 10 people with this and never got one complaint!! Happy cooking!!

I chose to sear the pork chop on the stove with a little olive oil and garlic salt before adding them to the dish. This helps keep the pork tender and juicy. I did follow the advice of microwaving the potatoes and am glad I did. Enjoy!

This was so good! I scaled it down to 3 servings as it's just my fiancé and I and it was the perfect amount. Luckily I had read the reviews prior to making this so I microwaved my potatoes for ten minutes, then mixed the cheese and onion in with them before putting them in the baking dish. I added the milk, then put in only 1 tbsp margarine before placing the chops, which I seasoned, on top. Finally, i added a little bit more milk over the chops, covered with foil and popped in the oven. After 30 minutes, I removed the foil and left in for the remaining 30 minutes. The potatoes were perfect and the pork chops were great. My fiancé was very happy with this dish and told me to add it to "the book"! Thank you so much for sharing!

This recipe was excellent! My husband loved it! I did microwave my potatoes for about 8 minutes prior to baking and this did help. I also added a heaping teaspoon of cornstarch to my milk to help thicken it. I then sprinkled garlic powder over the potatoes. I seasoned my pork chops on both sides with garlic salt and black pepper! It turned out delicious! I will certainly make this again! Thank you!

We thought this was very good! I followed other reviewers suggestions, and microwaved the potatoes for 10 minutes before putting them in the dish, and they came out perfectly cooked. I also seasoned with garlic salt. Thanks for the recipe!

I was excited to make this b/c of all the stuggles of others... a test of my culinary skills lol! Well it seemed that no one had much luck with the recipe as is I took reviewers advice along with my own thoughts. FIrst I thinly slices my potatos and nuked in milk for about 7 minutes. During that time I seasoned and seared my chops and put them on the bottem of my baking dish. I combined the the cheese and onions w/ potatoes and poured them on top, sprinkled with additional cheese. Baked covered for 30 minutes at 350, uncovered and was concerned about the potatoes. Baked it uncovered at 375 for the last 30. iT WAS GREAT! So I know we all haate some one who is totally changing the recipe and than rates it lol... but for so many issues some tweaking had to be done. 4 stars for the idea and the ingredients (which I used exacatly)!

Good, but I think it needs more cheese. Like other reviewers I cooked the potatoes in the microwave first (5 whole white potatoes at 8 minutes--almost fully cooked). I found mixing the ingredients ahead of time sort of difficult, as the cheese clumped into an unwieldly mess. Next time I won't pre-mix. I used boneless small pork chops which got too dry--I think--although everyone liked them. I baked in a convection oven at 350 for about 35 minutes. My kids refuse to eat onion, so I substituted with onion flakes and I added garlic powder to the potatoe mix. I topped the pork chops with steak seasoning. In the future, I'll add a bit of flour like others suggested, add more cheese, bake for less time, and only salt rather than steak season the pork chops. Other thoughts, I'm at about 6000 feet above sea-level. Thanks for the recipe!! We'll definitely make it again (there are few recipes that everyone in the family likes!)
Made it just as described. Did add paprika to the chops. It came out perfect.

Good basic recipe, with nice proportions. I added some sliced bell pepper, a few slices of tomato, and some small chunks of cream cheese. I made one pan with white potatoes and another with sweet potatoes, each turned out mellow. I seasoned the pork chops with hand-ground peppercorn, pink salt, paprika, and BBQ chicken seasoning.
I ended up with too much liquid? Would the use of 2% milk affect this recipe?
Milk curdled....

The pictures made it look better than it turned out. Took an hour and a half for the potatoes to cook enough. The end result was less than impressive. The sauce was watery and lacked flavor ( even though I tossed the potatoes with creole seasoning and pepper). I only used 2 pork chops, being a single person. Definitely wont be using this recipe again or recommending.
Followed the recipe. The potatos were delish but the pork chops were dry. Will chop remaining pork chops up to use in soup or beans

I followed directions exactly, however the cheese “sauce” did not thicken and I had a less than desirable outcome. It also took nearly an hour and a half to cook thoroughly. Really needed more flavor and a better cheese sauce recipe.

I only gave 3 stars because I felt it would have been helpful to be informed to not cover it. It occurs to me to cover it bc it cooks thoroughly and we are talking about pork. So fabulous ingredients. Ruined meal.

This was very good and an excellent way to keep the pork moist.
I had to cook the potatoes a lot longer than the hour recommend. And I halved the recipe!
